title: Corbel & Finch Elm Street closing letter
brief: Marguerite Pell, owner of Corbel & Finch Books, wants to write a letter to customers for the shop's website about closing the Elm Street store. Warm and honest, first person plural, no marketing gloss. Headings: "What is changing", "Why", "What stays the same", "How to say goodbye". The facts: the Elm Street shop, open for 17 years, closes for good after trading on 2026-12-23; the Harbor Road shop, the online shop and the school book fairs all continue; the reasons are that the Elm Street rent will rise 70 percent when the lease renews on 2027-01-01, and that more than half of sales now happen at Harbor Road or online, so the family chose to keep the two places that are growing; gift certificates and store credit are honored at Harbor Road and online until 2027-12-31; loyalty points move over automatically with nothing for customers to do; all stock at Elm Street is 20 percent off from 2026-11-28; the last Saturday story hour is on 2026-12-19 at 11:00, and a farewell evening with the staff and local authors is on 2026-12-22 from 17:00 to 20:00; the Elm Street team of 6 booksellers will move to Harbor Road, so the faces will be the same. Thank readers sincerely, and end with Marguerite's name.

edit.request: Change the closing date to 2026-12-30 and the discount to 30 percent, and add a sentence that the farewell evening will have a raffle to benefit the school book fairs.
